method: For each modern confirmed-event month, retrieve 6-minute NOAA PORTS currents at metadata real_time_bin for mb0302/mb0402/mb0501. Convert NOAA speed/direction to east/north vectors, integrate local 00:00-01:00/03:00/06:00, and compare the three-station mean eastward displacement on confirmed event dates with all complete calendar days in the same month. Background days remain unlabeled and are not treated as non-events.
decision: REJECT aggregate upper-bay eastward 6-hour displacement as a standalone Stage-2 predictive feature at this time. It is positive on the five event mornings, but four of five events are only at the 19th-48th percentile of same-month unlabeled background; only 2024-06-12 is elevated at about the 81st percentile. Directional sign alone is common and lacks specificity. Preserve local, vertical and phase-sensitive transport hypotheses instead.
interpretation: The positive-only event panel initially looked promising because all 15 modern station-event pairs were eastward over 6 hours. This same-month background comparison shows why that was insufficient: eastward upper-bay transport is common on ordinary/unlabeled summer mornings. The result is a useful falsification of a simple trigger feature and argues for location-specific, vertically resolved and phase-aware transport representation.
guardrails: Background calendar days remain UNLABELED, not clean non-event controls; unknown Jubilee contamination would bias the contrast toward the null.
This comparison does not estimate specificity, false-alert rate, calibration or causal effect.
Upper-bay PORTS currents are regional transport context, not Point Clear shoreline-current observations.
This result does not prove eastward transport is irrelevant; it rejects only the tested aggregate standalone representation.
No production feature, weight, threshold or forecast logic changed.
